analyst.summary: DLF has the best balance sheet it has had in a decade — net cash of over Rs 14,000 crore, growing rental income from its Cyber City/DLF-GIC rental business, and a rising dividend. But its own management guided flat home-sales bookings for FY27 (around Rs 20,000 crore, same as FY26, which itself was down 5% from the prior year's record), and said plainly it will not chase higher volumes the way competitors are. The stock, however, trades at a rich ~40x earnings and ~3.6x book value, with the market pricing in growth or a rental-business listing (REIT) that management has not committed to a timeline for. Delhi-NCR's home-buying market overall was the weakest of any major Indian city in the first half of 2026, though DLF's own Gurugram corridor is holding up better than most. Good company, but the price is asking for more than the guidance promises — Sell.
